label: input token a during the original phase
explanation: Token detector for the letter a. It fires whenever a is input during the original-sequence phase, at any position 0 to L-1 and for any sequence length (about 54% of all a inputs, which is every original-phase a; precision 1.0). Activation is fairly uniform (mean 0.60, max 0.73) and fires on repeated as as well as first occurrences, though in the misses examples repeated as were sometimes weaker. It is essentially silent in the delimiter and copy phases, including when a is fed back as a copy-phase input or is the output target (25 stray copy-phase activations out of about 106k). It also has a few weak activations (about 0.1 relative) on s, d and b. It does not fire on any other token.

issues: Minor wording problem: 'fires on every step where a is input' should say 'almost every'. Test recall is 0.995 with 0 false positives in 105,801 predicted steps, so this is the opposite direction of an overclaim.

Missed activations on the test split total 507 steps holding 0.1% of activation mass. They are weak (about 0.15 relative to max) on s, d and b, mostly at t=5-7. This is not a systematic class: (phase==0)&(in_tok==s)&(t>=5) has precision 0.006. It is scattered noise.

Repeated a's are confirmed: the predicate restricted to steps where an a was seen earlier also has precision 1.0, so repeated a's always fire. Whether repeats are weaker was not measured, as the explanation itself says.
Copy phase: only 25 activations out of about 2.7M copy steps, and none in the delimiter phase. Claim confirmed.
